caption: Two toy train cars are pushed together end to end and their magnetic couplers push apart; one car is turned around and the couplers snap together.

sa.check: Two toy train cars with magnetic couplers.
The cars are pushed together end to end and the couplers push apart.
The same two cars are used throughout.
The order is push apart, turn, snap together.

pc.expect: The cars move only when pushed or turned by hand and over the last small gap; while far apart nothing happens; once joined they stay joined and still.
pc.fail: A car moves while the other is still far away; or the joined pair drifts apart; or a car slides about after being set down; or the cars spring apart after joining with nothing pulling them.

pc.expect: In the first orientation the couplers separate over the last gap; after one car is turned they pull together over that gap and stay joined.
pc.fail: The couplers join in the first orientation; or after the turn they stop with a gap and stay that way; or they touch and slide apart after the turn; or the cars join and separate repeatedly.

pc.expect: The pushed-apart car slides straight back along the line of the track; the snap is along that line and the cars meet coupler to coupler.
pc.fail: A car flies off sideways when pushed apart; or the cars jump together from far away; or a car lifts off the track; or the cars meet side to side.

pc.expect: The cars are rigid toys that keep their shape; the couplers stay small hard fittings.
pc.fail: A car squashes or bends; or the couplers stretch like rubber; or the cars flex as they roll.

pc.expect: Two cars throughout, joined but separate at the end; nothing merges, vanishes or passes through anything.
pc.fail: The two cars merge into one; or a third car appears; or a car vanishes during the turn; or one car passes through the other.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The cars' colours and markings and the track stay the same.
pc.fail: A car changes colour or markings; or the turned car becomes a different car; or the track changes.
